subject.title: Feature request: Add Gateway received timestamp to inbound metadata for accurate latency tracking

question: Should OpenClaw expose Gateway receipt time as an agent-visible, plugin-SDK-backed inbound metadata field, and what stable name and timestamp format should become the contract?
rationale: Source inspection proves the field is missing, but choosing this public metadata/API shape affects all channel plugins and agent prompt semantics.

options.title: Expose `gatewayReceivedAt`
options.body: Add an additive receive-time field to the generic inbound context and render it in conversation metadata while preserving the existing source `timestamp`.

options.title: Diagnostics-only timing
options.body: Keep agent-visible metadata unchanged and expose receive-to-agent timing only through diagnostics, logs, or telemetry events.

options.title: Defer lifecycle timing design
options.body: Leave the issue open until a broader message-lifecycle observability schema chooses all receive, queue, agent-start, first-token, and send timing fields together.

recommendation.title: Expose `gatewayReceivedAt`
recommendation.body: Add an additive receive-time field to the generic inbound context and render it in conversation metadata while preserving the existing source `timestamp`.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing inbound metadata prompt surface and several relevant contract-shaping commits point to steipete as the strongest routing candidate.
